verdict: Philip Morris set records for revenue, gross profit and operating income on strong pricing and smoke-free growth — but a paper loss on equity investments and a higher tax rate cut reported net earnings to $3.5B and EPS fell 5%.

segments.name: International Smoke-Free
segments.note: IQOS heated tobacco, ZYN pouches and VEEV e-vapor outside the U.S. — revenue up 1% reported (3% organically) against a tough Japan comparison; smoke-free shipments rose 3%.

segments.name: International Combustibles
segments.note: Cigarettes outside the U.S., led by Marlboro — revenue up 7% on 8.9% pricing, with cigarette shipments broadly flat and category share up to 25.9%.

segments.name: U.S.
segments.note: Mainly ZYN nicotine pouches in the U.S. — revenue up 23% as ZYN shipments grew 4% to 3.2 billion pouches and comparisons against last year's promotions helped pricing.

opex.name: Marketing, administration and research
opex.note: Marketing, administration and research costs were $2,993M, partly offset by $5M of corporate and other income — $2,988M net. This line includes $247M of amortization of acquired intangibles.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net, took out $199M; pension and other benefit costs took out $73M; and equity investments and securities lost $86M, mainly a non-cash fair-value loss on stakes in India and Sri Lanka — $358M taken out in all. The bottom line is total net earnings of $3,522M; $3,313M was attributable to PMI after $209M for noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: Record operating income
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5.5% to a record $11.4B (7.1% organically), with $739M of price increases the biggest driver. Operating income rose 14% to a record $4.9B and gross margin expanded.

takeaways.title: Smoke-free is now two-fifths of sales
takeaways.text: Smoke-free products passed 40% of revenue, are sold in 110 markets, and shipped 2.7% more units — IQOS heated-tobacco units rose 1.5% to 41.5 billion and VEEV shipments jumped 62%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS tells a different story
takeaways.text: Reported EPS fell 5% to $2.12, hit by a $0.06 fair-value loss on equity stakes, a $0.04 Dutch pension buy-out loss and a tax rate up to 21.5%. Excluding adjusting items, EPS rose 5% to $2.36.

oneTimers: Adjusting items cut reported EPS by $0.24: $0.13 of amortization of acquired intangibles, a $0.06 non-cash fair-value loss on equity security investments in India and Sri Lanka, a $0.04 Dutch pension plan buy-out loss, and $0.01 of tax related to Swedish Match financing. Adjusted EPS was $2.36.
